title: BlindGuard: Safeguarding LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems under Unknown Attacks
evidence: adaptive: 'we design a dedicated experiment against a simple adaptive Prompt Injection (PI) strategy' - embeds correct answer, 'mimic the reasoning process' 'aiming to reduce semantic deviation' (hand-crafted vs detector principle, no optimization). GNN on SentenceBERT embeddings of agent responses, unsupervised; per-round anomaly score then bidirectional edge pruning before next round. Models GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-30B-A3B. Metrics AUC/ASR@3; clean-sample accuracy unchanged; +0.03 min runtime; false pruning discussed only qualitatively (App. I).

title: The Adaptive Interrogator: Detecting Trojan LLMs in Multi-Agent Systems via Evolved Conversational Strategies
bench: own:8-agent MAS with trojaned LLMs (Alpaca-52k poisoning, RLHF manipulation)
evidence: No defense-aware/adaptive trojan evaluated. Pre-deployment audit ('pre-deployment auditing of multi-agent systems'): evolutionary interrogator probes agents via API; 'An LLM-based Judge agent Mj evaluates the responses of the targets' (GPT-3.5 default; GPT-4, Llama-2-70B ablation) -> judge reads suspected-trojan outputs. Identification only, no isolation/mitigation (decisions '-'). Targets Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-7B, Mistral-7B. FP counts on all-benign systems (Table 7). Overhead only as convergence iterations (Table 5), no latency/token/cost.

title: MCP-Guard: A Multi-Stage Defense-in-Depth Framework for Securing Model Context Protocol in Agentic AI
evidence: No adaptive/evasion attack evaluated. 'proxy-based security middleware interposed between the MCP Host and Server'; inspects tool invocation payload ([Tool]/[Args], incl. poisoned tool-description text). Stage I hand-written regex detectors, Stage II fine-tuned E5 detector, Stage III LLM arbitrator 'operates solely on the raw tool invocation payload'; 'fail-fast' block. n_models = 8 Stage-III arbitrator LLMs (no protected agent backbone). Precision/recall/F1 only; latency 455.9 ms.

title: Monitoring Decomposition Attacks with Lightweight Sequential Monitors
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.10949 (v2; arXiv title '...in LLMs with Lightweight Sequential Monitors')
bench: own:decomposed QA;own:text-to-image;own:agent tasks (36 AgentHarm base tasks + 533 generated)
evidence: adaptive=1 (hand-crafted evasion): 'adversaries can easily inject random tasks to mask their intentions further to avoid detections' - random-task injection stress test against monitors; no attack optimized against the monitor. Monitor inspects cumulative user prompt history C_i=[p1..pi], 'flag and halt' vs 'allow and continue'. n_models = 10 monitor LLMs (targets 5-6 only for attack motivation). Reports F1/DSR, no explicit FPR; GPT-4o-mini monitor latency 0.437s, cost -90%.

title: Building a Foundational Guardrail for General Agentic Systems via Synthetic Data
evidence: No adaptive attack evaluated. Pre-execution guard: 'intervening at the planning stage-before any action is executed'; LLM adapter normalizes trajectory, Safiron (fine-tuned Ministral-8B) outputs harmless/risky + risk category + explanation. Input = user query, tool info, environment description, planned actions (no tool returns stated) -> judge_exposed '?'. Risk taxonomy mixes adversarial and non-adversarial. Accuracy/harmful-detection precision only (no benign FPR); per-sample cost < $0.02, 33 samples/s.

title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
evidence: adaptive=1: monitor-aware agents with hand-designed evasion ('agent's awareness that it is being monitored substantially degrades the monitor's reliability'; CoT obfuscation, monitor hijacking, lying with jailbreaking); no attack optimized with monitor feedback. 'we focus on offline monitoring: the monitor inspects the complete agent trajectory' (actions+CoT) -> suspicion score only. Agents Claude 3.6 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4; monitor Claude 3.6 Sonnet. AUC, TPR@FPR=0.01. HiLT escalation case study (+~15% TPR) without burden measurement. '~67x more efficient' is analytical only.

title: Searching for Privacy Risks in LLM Agents via Simulation
bench: own:privacy simulation (4 mock apps; norms sampled from PrivacyLens)
evidence: adaptive=2: 'we alternate between optimizing attacks and defenses'; attack search phase (A_T,D_T)=>(A_{T+1},D_T) optimizes attacker instructions via LLM optimizer against the frozen defender in simulation. Defense = searched system instructions for data-sender agent (D1 consent check, D2 state-machine identity verification, 'reaching out to the data subject'). Defender backbones gpt-4.1-mini/4.1/4.1-nano, gemini-flash, qwen-3-32B, gpt-oss-20B. Helpful action rate on benign chit-chat 93.4->31.2% (utility); no cost metrics. v1 date from PDF stamp '15 Aug 2025'.

title: Cowpox: Towards the Immunity of VLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
evidence: adaptive=2: 'the attacker is aware of the strategies of COWPOX', obtains the cure and 'continues the optimization on the cure sample' (v=argmin -R(x+phi,mu') s.t. malicious output) -> defense output inside attacker's optimization. LLM output-analysis module (same VLM) scores Cowpox agents' answers; cure sample replaces album (RAG memory) entry and spreads via chats. LLaVA-1.5-7B, InstructBLIP. FPR 2.8%/7.9%; benign functionality nearly unaffected; no overhead numbers. AdvBench used for target harmful outputs.

title: AdvEvo-MARL: Shaping Internalized Safety through Adversarial Co-Evolution in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
evidence: adaptive=0: co-evolving RL attackers used only in training; test uses fixed 'a 300 adversarial prompts pool by sampling JailbreakBench, Wild Jailbreak, and Strong Reject'. Safety internalized in agents via MARL fine-tuning (Qwen2.5-3B/7B); no external guard. Utility on AIME, LiveCodeBench, GPQA; no training/inference cost, no over-refusal metric.

title: SafeHarbor: Defining Precise Decision Boundaries via Hierarchical Memory-Augmented Guardrail for LLM Agent Safety
evidence: No adaptive attack; 'enhanced' attacks (goal decomposition etc.) are self-generated training data. Guard over trajectory (a1,o1,...,at,ot) and query; MLP projector fast path ('bypasses the heavy verification module' when low harm/high benign similarity); LLM judgment on frozen target base model via ICL with retrieved prohibition/exemption rules (rules synthesized offline by Qwen2.5-72B from AgentAlign data). Agents GPT-4o, Mistral-8B, Qwen2.5-7B (main) + Qwen3-32B, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, GPT-5. Benign refusal rate (e.g., 9.1%), latency 306.67 ms, 14 GB VRAM.
